claims.text: A tailored post-solidification heat treatment can induce controlled short-range chemical order in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
MoNbTaW or HfMoNbTaW can serve as homogeneous, single-phase refractory high-entropy alloy starting materials.
Short-range order modifies the local chemical landscape experienced by dislocations.
Short-range order reduces the rate of double-kink nucleation in screw dislocations.
Short-range order promotes cross-slip locking in screw dislocations.
Induced short-range order shifts the dominant deformation mechanism from screw dislocations toward edge dislocations.
A change in deformation mode from screw to edge dislocations can contribute an edge-dislocation-induced strengthening mechanism in HfMoNbTaW.
Combining solid-solution strengthening with edge-dislocation-induced strengthening improves high-temperature yield strength.
An SRO-inducing treatment will produce significantly higher yield strength than processing without induced SRO.
The SRO-induced yield-strength improvement will persist throughout 800°C to 1600°C.
The influence of SRO on dislocation mobility remains beneficial up to 1600°C.
The 800°C to 1600°C range is relevant to high-temperature refractory-alloy applications.
High-strength refractory high-entropy alloys are relevant to aerospace vehicles and nuclear reactors.
The effect of SRO on screw and edge mobility becomes attenuated as temperature increases.
The optimal degree of SRO for maximum strength and its long-term service stability are undetermined.
Poorly selected thermal-treatment parameters may cause detrimental phase changes.

contradictions.description: The stated comparator is a fully homogenized or conventionally processed chemically homogeneous alloy, whereas the proposed experiment uses an as-solidified control. As-solidified and fully homogenized conditions can differ in segregation, defect state, grain structure, and pre-existing order, so the experimental control does not unambiguously implement the stated baseline.
